external_coverage.exact_statement: Let K be any complete non-Archimedean real-valued field and L a semiample rational line bundle on a projective K-scheme. The decreasing-FS-net psh class is closed under finite maxima and real constant shifts. Every such psh metric admits a decreasing smooth semipositive approximation net, uniform when its endpoint is continuous. (BE2021v3, §§7.1 and 7.3.)

For an n-dimensional projective scheme over any complete non-Archimedean real-valued field and rational line bundles L1,…,Ln, the smooth semipositive mixed curvature measure extends uniquely to continuous psh-regularizable metrics, continuously for uniform metric convergence and weak Radon convergence. The extension is positive, symmetric and multiadditive, with raw intersection mass (L1⋯Ln). (BE2021v3, Theorem 8.4 and Proposition 8.5.)

On a good Hausdorff pure n-dimensional boundaryless analytic space over a complete non-Archimedean field, smooth symmetric forms α of type (p,p) and β of type (q,q), with p+q=n−1 and compact support intersection, satisfy ∫α∧d′d″β=∫d′d″α∧β. (CLD2012v1, Theorem 3.12.2.)

Over any complete non-Archimedean field, on a good Hausdorff pure n-dimensional analytic space, n locally psh-approachable functions have a unique positive Radon top product on the interior, continuous under uniform smooth psh approximation against compact smooth tests, symmetric, multilinear and compatible with restrictions; it extends to differences of approachable functions. (CLD2012v1, §5.6.)

On good Hausdorff analytic spaces over a complete non-Archimedean field, compact sets admit smooth cutoffs in prescribed open neighborhoods; compact continuous tests admit uniformly approximating smooth tests there; positive Radon measures on the interior correspond bijectively to positive top currents. (CLD2012v1, §3.3 and Proposition 5.4.6.)

For topologically locally trivial continuous metrized line bundles on good Hausdorff pure-dimensional boundaryless analytic spaces over a complete non-Archimedean field, local weight curvatures glue independently of trivialization, since d′d″log|h|=0 for analytic units h. (CLD2012v1, §6.4.1.)

Over any complete non-Archimedean field, the analytification of a separated finite-type scheme is good, Hausdorff and without boundary; if the scheme is proper, its analytification is compact. (Berkovich, Non-archimedean analytic spaces, Trieste 2009 notes, Definition 3.2.9 and Facts 4.1.1–4.1.4.)
